Why were you rummaging around in odd places? What are you hiding?
Nothing. When I'm taken by surprise I sort of, ah, make strange noises.
Please don't tell anyone about what you saw. It'll be such an embarrassment to Guildenstern and me.
We weren't up to anything nefarious. I promise. Just errands for, ah, a friend. Hrrk...
Why were you rummaging around in odd places? What are you up to?
Hmm! Who wants ta' know?
Me. I want to know.
Well, it's a secret!
I witnessed Lady Rosencrantz and Guildenstern rummaging around in odd places. You were saying, about a spy...?
(Could it be... they're loyal to another above me?)
I'll ask Bernardo to interrogate them shortly. Thank you for your vigilance, Ophelia.
I saw Lady Rosencrantz and Guildenstern acting in a most peculiar way. Could they be the spies you're looking for?
Although they are outsiders to Elsinore, they have been long-time friends of Hamlet's. And they appear to have little interest in Danish affairs.
Or any affairs, anywhere, for that matter.
I'll speak to them, at the very least. Thank you for your vigilance, Ophelia.
Do you know why Queen Gertrude might be rummaging through her husband's things in secret?
I don't know what she might be looking for, if that's what you're asking.
But I... understand why she might not want to simply ask him directly.
Let me only say that there are secrets between King Claudius and Queen Gertrude.
I suspect all marriages are prone to a little secrecy here and there, perhaps.
I wouldn't know, never having been wed myself.
Your mother was searching through your uncle's belongings. Do you know what she might have been looking for?
After all I've learned about her other schemes lately, I hardly care anymore.
Proof, perhaps.
You mean of your father's murder?
Yes. But I doubt her loyalties, and I doubt my assessment of those loyalties.
So I shall not speak to her of it.
Of something larger than either of us. But I doubt her loyalties, and I doubt my assessment of those loyalties.
So I shall not speak to her of it, lest I be revealed.
Queen Gertrude was looking through the King's personal belongings. I don't think he knew it was happening.
Well, only seems fair, considering I do that to her all the time. Her private diary is something special!
Is it really wise of you to come out and admit that?
I'm bored to tears. All I do is wait on Gertrude and help her choose her next soiree gown. Where else am I supposed to find fulfillment?
My lady, I saw you looking through the King's personal belongings. I know.
You-- you did?
What were you doing, if you don't mind my asking?
I do mind, in fact.
It was something very personal, Ophelia. Something I'd like my husband and I to keep between us.
But rest assured, it was no threat to anyone. Not even to him.
My lady told me of this. She is searching for something private. Something which was taken.
Her husband promised her their life would be one of openness, of honesty, of communication.
After so many years with Hamlet-- he was so terribly cold to her.
But Claudius lies to her now in just the same way. Is this the fate of all men with a little power?
My lady is a powerful woman in her own right. She has the blood in her to rule empires. Why is she reduced to digging through a man's closet?
I saw the Queen rummaging through your things.
Yes. Bernardo is addressing it anon. What comes of my wife's dealings is none of your business.
You saw my wife? You're certain?
As the day is long, my lord.
How odd. I inquired with my wife directly, assuming she would naturally have been in my chambers. And yet, she denied it.
I'll... have Bernardo speak to her privately. This is... disconcerting.
I saw the Queen rummaging through the King's things in an odd, hurried way.
Yes. We're addressing it anon. The King is aware - fear not.
The Queen is the one who went through his private items?
But... he asked her directly, and she denied it..
Ophelia, this is a very serious allegation. If it's true...
Then it means the Queen has lied to her husband directly.
I must bring her in and ask her some questions, I think. I'll notify the King.
I saw Bernardo sneaking out of the castle in the early morning hours. You were saying, about a spy...?
You saw that? Hah! No, you needn't worry about him.
Then where is he going, my lord?
Nowhere holy or wholesome. That's all you need to know.
But I've nothing to fear from Bernardo. No—him least of all.
I saw Bernardo sneaking out of the castle in the early morning hours.
Yes. Well.
As far as all that, let's simply say it's none of our concern at the moment.
Not unless Bernardo would like to discuss any of it further.
You mean... about Katherine?
Ah. So you've learned already.
I suspect it's been causing him no small amount of anguish.
Luckily, all that will be resolved soon enough. Bernardo and I are planning to leave town.
Please don't tell anyone.
I won't. I'd suspected something like that might happen.
If Katherine ever wants to express herself fully, she's going to need to do it somewhere better. Happier.
Far away from this sad place.
Do you think it'd help Bernardo if someone went and spoke to him about all this?
Perhaps it's worth a try.
You're the most even-keeled among us. If you can't make Bernardo's life easier, no one can.
I do declare, Ophelia. That's the nicest compliment anyone's ever paid me. I shall try to live up to it.
I saw Bernardo sneaking out of the castle in the early morning hours. What do you know?
Ahhhh, feckin' hell! Only that he's up to no good!
He always makes me take 'is post in his place.
Dunno if it's wine, women, or that other 'w' word. What's the one...
...Waltzing? Wealth?
Whortleberries! That's th' one.
You don' know 'em? All the guards collect 'em in the forest. Then they make pies. We love 'em!
Yeh haven't truly lived until you've had a whortleberry pie with a big ol' mug of whortleberry wine!
I'll have to take your word on that one.
Bernardo, I overheard some mention of your business in town.
Well, you know precisely what.
Oh. I suppose I do, don't I? It all makes sense, now.
...It's nothing very interesting. I can assure you of that.
I would give you the details, but it's quite a long and boring story. It is in your best interest that I spare you.
Have you seen the Guard Captain, Bernardo? Perhaps late in the evening?
Yes. That person has amassed quite the name around here. A rare talent.
But I'm afraid that's all I'm able to say on the matter.
I saw my father burning some documents in his room. You were saying, about a spy...?
Documents? Of what origin?
No... Hrm. It matters not. Whatever he has to hide... all roads must be pursued.
I'll have Bernardo bring your father in for a conversation immediately.
Yes, Bernardo made his treachery clear. I'm thankful that you caught him in the act.
Hopefully some time in a cell will give him a better understanding of his position.
Father, I know you were burning some secretive documents in your room. Can you explain why?
I expected never to speak of them again. And now, I won't.
Those horrid notes are gone forever. And good riddance.
Love, please don't tell anyone about what you saw. Please. It could mean my head.
(Ah. Right. He hasn't burned them yet in this world.)
I don't know what you mean, my love. Don't worry your head over it.
I saw my father burning some documents in his room. The King was saying earlier, about a spy...?
In and of itself, that's not troubling, but I'd like to see him about it regardless.
I'll bring him in for questioning immediately. Thank you for your attentiveness, Ophelia.
Laertes, I saw Father burning something in his chambers late at night. Notes of some sort. Do you know what they were?
I don't.
But do you not trust Father to know what is right in these matters?
I do, but-- I also think those notes contain something important.
If you were to describe what you saw to the wrong people, it would put Father-- and both of us-- in grave danger.
I understand you're curious, Ophelia. But family comes first. Whatever Father was doing, I'm certain he was correct to do so.
What if you bring down suspicion upon him in this climate, and it turns out to have been nothing much at all? Won't you feel silly then?
Bernardo would like to meet with you privately. Could you report to him, please?
This is very sudden... are you certain, my lady? I-if it is your request, of course...
T...this is an insult! How dare he waste my time!
I'm going to give him a piece of my mind.
Ha. Yes, Ophelia, I'll play along.
Come to think of it, I did see something strange. I'll tell him of it.
If he insists. Whatever can he want from me now?
O-of course, at once! I must wonder... why he didn't come to me himself? Oh, bother it, never mind...
Well, of course. I wonder what he's so keen about?
Oh, 'sblood, what have I done now? Mus' be somethin' worth scoldin' me for...
Hah! I no longer take orders from you.
Charming... but I don't answer to you any more, love.
If the good Guard Captain wishes it, then so may it be, of course. Hee hee!
Really? The Guard Captain and I already spoke earlier today.
I think he's heard all he needs to from me today.
Of course. Did he say what it was about?—Ah, I suppose it matters little. I'll see him shortly.
Oh, goodness. Whatever have I done now?
Yes, of course, I'll find him when I'm able.
We've already met him. Guilda dragged me along after you told her the same thing.
We've already met him. Don't you remember? We went to prison.
I think we've been questioned quite enough.
Tell him I didn't steal it! I was only, ahem, borrowing it indefinitely!
Steal what?
Oh, so this isn't about any of the things I've pilfered?
Guilda, you've only been in Elsinore for a little while. How many things did you borrow indefinitely?
Guilda, you haven't even reached the castle yet. How many things did you borrow indefinitely?
Hmm. I so hate doing sums in my head. Let's not worry about the precise numbers here.
Regardless, I shall meet with Bernardo whenever I can pencil the good Guard Captain into my busy schedule!
Ummm... no, thank you.
I already met with him once, with Rosey. I've done my part!
I even went to jail! Absolutely <i>no interest<i> in doing that again.
Horatio, do you know about Bernardo's performance career?
...As Katherine, I mean. Bernardo plays a woman in town performances.
Oh, of course.
Isn't she just fantastic? I caught a show last week.
How could you already know about it?
Honestly, Ophelia, I'm mildly offended you even have to ask. I adore the arts. And Elsinore is where culture goes to die.
Thus, I must go into town to satiate myself. Katherine's stage makeup is good, but it isn't that good.
I don't think she's ever noticed me among the crowd. I keep to myself.
Well, Bernardo-- or Katherine-- is more than a little tormented over others finding out about this.
So you... immediately... ran to... come tell me and everyone else you know?
No! Well, you. I thought you might be able to help Bernardo, for precisely the reason you mentioned.
I'm just trying to find someone Bernardo can talk to.
You've traveled all over and met all kinds of people. Have you ever met anyone like Bernardo?
Putting aside my utter disgust at you for the moment... yes, many a time.
My dear, I have just the thing to cure this forlorn spirit. Allow me to handle this.
May I speak with you?
About you as Katherine.
As I said before, please don't tell anyone anything, and let me handle the matter.
I understand. And I'll heed that. But I'd like you to know something, too.
I also know this might seem sudden, and strange. But I want you to know once more that I have your back.
And that I am, as always, your faithful friend. No matter how you want to be called.
It's been a strange life, this one.
I never meant for you to find out, truth be told.
I thought I could keep the two parts of me separated. As though we were different people.
But the pressure of it felt like I was being ripped in two.
No one can live like that forever.
I'm glad I can be honest with you, Ophelia. Thank you.
Certainly. What about?
I know that you go by both Bernardo and Katherine.
I also know this might seem sudden, and strange. But I want you to know that I have your back.
I-I'm afraid I don't know what you mean. It's...
Please, ah, please pardon me, Ophelia. But I really must go.
Whatever you think you saw, please don't tell anyone.
(Hmm. I don't think it was wise of me to spring the news like that.)
Do you know where Bernardo goes at night?
Is... it bad news?
No. Merely worth sharing.
Bernardo performs in a theater troupe, where he performs as a woman: Katherine.
I often thought... well... er... suspected...
Never mind it.
I must speak to him immediately.
Ahh, I see the news has broken at last. A good secret can only stay hidden so long!
Yes, I've been keeping the good captain's dirty little secret under hat. But really, Lady Ophelia, I was doing him a service.
Can you imagine the fresh hell it would raise if Marcellus and the other guards found out? Or his friends?
If I really wanted to shame Bernardo, I would have told the other men a long time ago.
Who do you think you can trust with something like that, girl? I implore you to find out, both to sate your curiosity and mine.
...The bar?
Ah, no, never mind it. I forgot he'd given up drink a while back. That pious fool. Honestly.
He performs with an amateur theater troupe in town, as a woman. Katherine.
One of those sorts of players?
How did he never... how did I never know?
I wish I had time to discuss this with him, but my ship is about to depart.
Still, sister, I urge you to be silent on this matter.
And he never told me. No. I won't stand for it.
I must speak with him as soon as possible.
Bernardo believes there might be a spy in the castle. What do you know?
Well, there's Guilda and I. The King asked us to sort of keep an eye on Hamlet.
I mean something more nefarious. An attempt by Norway to meddle in Danish affairs, that sort of thing.
Oh. Well, Guilda likes to pretend to be a multinational spy at inns when she's had too much to drink...
It hasn't exactly made us many friends.
But I don't think that's what you mean here. So no, I've not heard anything, but shall let you know if I do.
Me! It's me!
Yes, I'm the Norwegian spy! I just couldn't help but lend myself to Norway's cause.
On account of Prince Fortinbras being so dre-e-e-eamy, and all. I'd kill a hundred men for him!
Guilda, this isn't a make-believe scenario.
Oh. It isn't?
Well, then. That's no fun. I thought we were pretending.
Hmm, speaking of pretending...
Don't forget that once I start hiding, you'll need to invite absolutely everyone to my funeral!
Show me someone who isn't a spy in this castle, and I'll show you a fool or a corpse.
Very funny. But truly--have you seen anything... suspicious?
If I had, that would be our good friend Bernardo's little problem, wouldn't it?
Although, come to think of it...
It's likely nothing. Something odd. I'll speak to Bernardo about it when I can.
Bernardo believes a spy may be hiding in Elsinore. What do you know?
Oh, of course! Ask the dark-skinned outsider what he knows of spies and treachery.
I... I didn't mean it that way, Horatio. I merely wanted to know if you had information I didn't.
My apologies, Ophelia. I'm a bit on edge. I can sense the bluebloods of this castle looking at me sidelong and clutching their bosoms with fear.
Luckily, the good Bernardo believes I'm pure of heart... for now. And as he's running the investigation, his opinion is the only one that matters.
Still, if you haven't spoken to him, perhaps you ought to. Just to set your mind at ease.
Bernardo believes a foreign spy may be embedded in Elsinore. What do you know?
Why must the spy be foreign? Why not someone with hatred of the throne?
Many would see a knife in my lady's back. Many would slit her husbands' throats.
Many people wanted my lady dead, I'm certain, for the simple reason of her station.
But the true threat is under their very noses, in the last place they look.
And who might that be?
My lady listens to nothing I say... but that boy... he will be the end of her. And Claudius, too.
My lady listens to nothing I say... but that boy... he will be the end of her.
Who is to say where the boy goes at night and to whom he speaks? He's friends with that snake-whisperer of a scholar, that Horatio!
What are the two of them doing constantly? That's what I want to know!
Bernardo believes a spy in Elsinore. Have you seen anything amiss?
I... I'm afraid I try not to think about these sorts of things right now, Ophelia.
If you've seen anything amiss...
Then I urge you to go to Captain Bernardo and tell him, of course. That's his profession—not mine.
Of course, my lady.
I've heard the news about a spy in Elsinore. What do you know?
Ah. You've heard of that already? Did Voltemand tell you?
Despite how worrying it may sound, I feel certain the danger to you is very little, my lady.
I don't care about that. I want information. What can you tell me?
It is an ongoing investigation. At the moment, it is up to myself and my men to get to the bottom of it.
I never expected to need to arrest your father, of all people. So this really is a strange and sensitive circumstance.
I never expected to need to arrest Hamlet's schoolmates, of all people. So this really is a strange and sensitive circumstance.
I've been asking all with suspicious information to report it to me. That is—if you think someone knows something about all this...
Tell them I've requested a meeting with them.
I'll interrogate them further. Politely, of course.
My lord, I'd like to discuss the rumors of a spy in Elsinore Castle.
A spy?
Pah hah hah! Wherever did you hear a story like that?
(Ah, right. He hasn't found out about it yet.)
Yes? And what of them?
Have you seen something awry?
If you have cause for suspicion, speak to Captain Bernardo immediately. He has my explicit trust in handling this matter swiftly.
Bernardo's found the traitor. I think that puts an end to the matter for the time being. Don't you?
What news are you talking about? You're making that up, aren't you?
Classic. Your life is so boring, you have to invent some flair.
(Ah, right. No one in the castle knows about the spy yet.)
As much as you do, 'Feely.
I must admit, Claudius's constant paranoia gets tiresome. I don't know how the Queen stands it!
Powerful men can be so odd. Did you hear about the last King of England? Some said he was madder than Hamlet.
He even had his pretty young wife killed. In public! With the way Claudius has been carrying on lately...
Anyhow, isn't it Bernardo's occupation to worry about such things? Bother him, why don't you?
Father, I heard the worrying news about a spy in the castle.
A spy? Where? Who told you?
(Ah. Right. Morning court hasn't happened yet—they don't know.)
I, er, overheard Bernardo discussing it.
I see. I certainly find the notion very interesting, but not substantial as of yet.
You don't think there's a spy going around after all?
Oh... I'm not saying that necessarily, dearest. Everyone's on high alert lately. Suspicions are running high.
I find it odd, but not noteworthy unless some evidence turns up to reinforce this rumor.
Regardless, if you see anything concerning, I urge you to speak with the good guard captain Bernardo about this. He can put your mind at ease.
Hamlet is going to try to overthrow Grace and escape. He intends for you and Guilda to perish.
What? That couldn't be so.
Although, given Hamlet's mood swings as of late...
I suppose it wouldn't be surprising. How can you know this?
He told me himself. He asked that I be ready to escape with him.
Evidently he really has forgotten us.
Thank you for informing us. We'll keep a close watch.
Hamlet is going to try to overthrow Grace and escape. He intends for you and Rosencrantz to perish.
What? How d'you know that?
Y-you think he'd let us die?
But... he's our friend!
This was all supposed to be a relaxing trip. But all of us might die... how's anyone supposed to relax like that?
It's murder on all sides, Ophelia. It's murder soup. Served ice cold!
Even on the open sea, everyone's trying to have everyone else killed.
I felt you ought to know, in the interest of protecting yourself.
Thanks for telling me. Rosie and I will keep a look-out.
So. This plan of yours.
Can you not clear up any misconceptions with Lady Rosencrantz and Lady Guildenstern?
Misconceptions? Ophelia, they were carrying my death warrant.
I can bear no further trust for them.
They seem so... guileless. How could they be plotting your death?
All women seem so guileless. Hardly any are truly as harmless as they seem.
They may seem like idle gossips, but there's steel in both of them. I'm keeping my distance.
Keep an eye out. My mutiny begins shortly.
About what?
I know about the plan you're hatching. The one to overthrow Grace.
How, exactly, can you know that?
You're not as opaque as you think you are.
I also suspect your contingency plan. You'd trade my life for Rosie and Guilda's if it came to it, wouldn't you?
Well, of course.
But if you've come here to dissuade me, you won't change my mind about that.
Prince Hamlet has a plan to retaliate against you violently. I'd be willing to share details...
Does he, now? Do tell.
I see. Fascinatin'. Thank yeh much, lady.
I've much respect for those whose hearts I can trust. I won' forget this.
I heard you speaking of your adventures. Can you... tell me more?
Certainly. Though I must admit, the bulk of my tales are to an audience.
I'll have to charge you a very steep price if you want a private story.
I've got a little coin on me—
I was talking about your company and private conversation. The attention of a fair woman is all the prize in the world.
I... that wouldn't be proper. We haven't even met before.
What's to know? I'm Othello, humble barkeep. And you, of course, are the lady Ophelia—I've seen your brother, too.
Why should the black sheep not flock together?
Ah... I didn't know I was so well-known.
Of course. And the subject of some mystery, too! Hardly anyone in town has laid eyes on you. And now I've met you for myself.
If the sad old tales of a washed-up sailor are of interest to one as fair as you, come see me at midnight, when the bar closes.
We'll speak further then.
I hear you've been beset by thugs as of late.
It would appear my fortune has quickly changed.
I was warned that the castle guard has decided to make their presence known in town, in order to protect me.
Rumor has it a young noblewoman pleaded my case to them. I wonder who that might be?
If you'd be so inclined, I'd like to speak with you in private later this evening.
Both to extend my deepest gratitude... and to get to know the fair woman to whom I owe my life and limb.
The bar closes at midnight. Meet me then.
I'll make do.
That wasn't what I asked. Haven't you asked the city guard for assistance?
You should well know, my lady, that the guard doesn't help people like us.
To them, we look better smeared beneath their heels.
I... Listen. I know some of them personally. Maybe they'll help me.
Othello the Barkeep seems to be in trouble.
Yes. It's been that way nearly ever since he moved here.
Vile insects that won't leave the poor man alone!
Their violence upon him is new, and I fear it will grow worse. But Castle Town is an outside world.
I do not meddle in its affairs, nor it in mine.
But don't you think there's some way we could help him?
Something-- anything?
The good Guard Captain may have the answer you seek.
Bernardo demonstrates remarkable softness whenever it comes to your requests.
Othello's in trouble. Can you help?
Me? What do you think I can do?
You could help defend his inn. I've seen you fight. You were a soldier once.
O-Ophelia, that isn't how this works.
I'm no Dane. I'm merely passing through. Inviting that kind of attention could be very dangerous for me.
Othello's a good man, and I care for him greatly, and he serves good wine, but...
But you're afraid to get involved.
Yes. And so should you be.
Othello's in trouble. Can you assist?
Oh, my, no. What do I look like to you? A personal army?
I've never even held a weapon before. It is my belief that the pointed side goes outwards...
But one can never truly be certain, can they?
I fear Othello will simply have to work out his woes on his own.
What would you like me to do?
Help me find someone who can make sure Othello's bar is defended.
Ah. Well. Allow me to share this helpful technique for doing just that.
Whenever I'm in need of assistance, I simply go to the most crowded location I can find.
Then I lie face down on the ground, and I scream.
It's had a one hundred percent success rate of people inquiring as to whether I need help.
I-- I don't think this is the kind of help they mean.
Really? I've never said 'yes' before, so I wouldn't know. The pure joy of the cry for help is enough for me.
Othello the Barkeep has been beset by thugs. He needs assistance from the Castle.
Wah! That sorry ol' man's twice a thug over himself!
The way I see it, innocent people in Castle Town are being threatened and have no recourse.
M'lady, we don't... ah... get involved in those kinds o' matters.
Marcellus, please. I'm begging you to get involved in this one. He needs help.
F-f-fine! Fine. Stop lookin' at me wiv those big green eyes! Yer just like yer damn mother!
Othello, the barkeep in town, has been beset by thugs. Can't you do anything?
We don't ordinarily have jurisdiction over the town.
I know Othello. He ought to ask his local guards for protection.
He's tried. None of them will stand by him.
And how did you hear about this man's case, exactly? How do you know Othello?
I... he... well...
Ophelia! You've been rummaging around in town alone? With that barkeep?
Well, now I'm obligated to send Marcellus down for your own safety, if you're making friends with criminals.
My lady, be aware you are making things very difficult for all of us.
Be safe. Please.
I will. You have my word. I just want to make sure he's all right.
My lord, you know of Hamlet's affections for me. Do you bear me any ill will as a result?
Wah hah hah! No. I care not a whit what Hamlet feels on this front. His feelings don't factor in here.
In fact, I'm about to arrange a suitable match for him with Lady Birgitta.
We've been holding back on the betrothal because of the war effort, but we should move quickly now that we have reached tentative peace.
In fact, I was about to arrange a match between Hamlet and Lady Birgitta, before she proved herself a liar.
There are, of course, other suitable candidates in the wings.
None of them you, naturally.
Well, no, of course not. Right now, I trust you implicitly. How could I ever mean to do you harm?
I didn't think so.
My lady, you know of Hamlet's affections for me. Do you believe the King finds me inconvenient?
What? No! Absolutely not!
Ophelia... it hurts my heart to hear you even suggest such a thing.
Please, don't take it as an offense that he disapproves of a union between you and my son.
He is trying to make the best match possible, and we have only one heir, after all. It can sometimes be an inscrutable process.
In fact, my husband is about to arrange a suitable match for him with Lady Birgitta.
He'll arrange for a meeting between them soon.
Brit, do you believe King Claudius truly wants me dead because of my prior relationship with Hamlet?
Since you know the truth about me -- No. Not a chance. Who told you that rubbish?
Well, you did, to my brother. Offhand.
Hmm. Did I? That was to persuade him, I think.
But no -- I don't believe that for an instant. Claudius is far too dull to play chess like that.
No, 'Feely, I have-- had, at least-- a special monopoly on wanting you dead.
I think you're safe for the time being. I seem to have lost my nerve.
Maybe. Maybe not.
Why? Is there something ominous happening in your personal life?
Something's got you looking over your shoulder? If so, do tell.
Hamlet, I believe your uncle may want me dead because of our 'history' together.
I fear he wishes to make a more appropriate match with you. Lady Brit, perhaps.
I fear he wishes to make a more advantageous match with you.
And... I'm an obstacle to that.
My father's ghost warned me of this. It told me Claudius was a killer.
My father's ghost appeared before me on the walls. It warned me about this. It told me Claudius was a killer.
I believe you, Hamlet.
And now you tell me my uncle intends to take your life, too.
It's... almost too much to bear.
Not while I live.
I'll not allow him to harm you.
This only adds conviction to my crime. I shall do the world a favor.
...I can see only blood ahead of me.
For now, let me play the part he expects of me. But soon, Ophelia, he'll be gone.
And then he'll trouble you no more. I swear it.
For my own sanity, I must find out if my mother knew of this. I have to know if she was complicit, too.
Father, you know of Hamlet's affections for me. Couldn't this be cause for the King to harm me?
Why do you ask? Did something happen?
Do you have reason to believe you might be... harmed?
